A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title. All 12 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–B, and both algorithms, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original leakage measurements, encoder validation-loss curves, and decoding experiments on Narratives and ZuCo in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original leakage measurements and decoding experiments in Tables 1–4 and the encoder validation-loss curves in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The core graph procedure and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. However, v3's new Appendix B walkthrough says to split the fMRI graph by subjects U, whereas retained Algorithm 2, line 28, specifies tasks V. The PDFs do not resolve whether this indicates an intended procedural revision or an explanatory error.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Narratives fMRI-to-text and ZuCo1.0 EEG-to-text decoding with the same represented populations and tasks. Dataset descriptions move from Section 4.1 to Appendix A. Newly discussed subject-specific and brain-to-image work supplies context, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same splitting methods and models: UniCoRN, randomly initialized-encoder UniCoRN*, and EEG2Text. The fMRI decoder comparisons retain methods (a)–(e), and EEG retains (a), (c), and (d). Newly cited models such as DeWave are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported 80/10/10 partition ratio, preprocessing, window length, training configurations, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. CSLR becomes BSLR without a formula change. v3 explains the existing EEG comparator exclusions; its ROUGE header changes do not establish a different evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same random-encoder ablation, learning-rate and training-duration comparisons, and encoder validation-loss analysis. v1 Figure 3 is retained as v3 Figure 4. No additional experimental analysis accompanies the new EEG2Text sentence in Limitations.

E5.justification: Both versions report four seeds, seed-specific leakage measurements, and averages. v3 Appendix A newly identifies the actual seed values as 1, 2, 3, and 4. This is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of increased runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical table entries and plotted curves are retained, but Tables 2–4 swap ROUGE headings from F/P/R to R/P/F without rearranging values. For example, Table 4 assigns Narratives UniCoRN F=15.55 in v1 and F=19.04 in v3; this is changed metric attribution, not a demonstrated performance gain. v3 also newly attributes persistent encoder overfitting specifically to EEG2Text in Limitations.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces v1's matched-pair split definitions with a Cartesian-product definition and auxiliary signal, subject-index, and text sets in v3 Equations 1–4. The product does not explicitly restrict combinations to observed signal–text pairs, creating a substantive formal ambiguity. The remaining mathematical content adds no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly scopes the contribution to cross-subject splitting and foregrounds dataset utilization alongside generalization. The novelty statement changes from the first contamination-free splitting method to the first cross-subject splitting criterion. The central leakage diagnosis, proposed separation rules, and fair-benchmark contribution remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds arguments connecting subject-specific training to wasted data, individual anatomical variability, and overfitting on limited data. It also explicitly presents persistent EEG2Text encoder overfitting as an unresolved limitation. The principal leakage interpretation and the caveat about discarding data are retained.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix A supplies exact seed values, and Appendix B adds an explicit fMRI graph walkthrough, although that walkthrough conflicts with retained pseudocode. Filtering references, hardware, batch sizes, learning-rate schedules, training durations, window length, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially repositions the work against subject-specific decoding, citing Tang and Ye, and connects it to cross-subject brain-to-image research by Wang and Liu. DeWave is also added, while broad BCI and neural-translation references are removed. These changes rebuild the research-positioning argument rather than merely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten, with terminology revised throughout. Experimental settings and results become separate sections, dataset descriptions move into Appendix A, Appendix B expands, and acknowledgements are removed. This substantially changes the narrative and organization despite stable experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1's encoder–decoder schematic is replaced by a dataset-structure illustration, and Figure 2's legend is redesigned. The existing appendix splitting diagram moves into the main text as Figure 3; the unchanged loss plot becomes Figure 4. Tables retain their structure apart from revised labels, including the ROUGE headings.

improvement.justification: v3 improves orientation through explicit cross-subject framing, clearer section organization, and exact seed disclosure. However, it introduces an unexplained reassignment of ROUGE values, an fMRI walkthrough contradicting Algorithm 2, and a Cartesian-product definition lacking an explicit observed-pair restriction. These technical ambiguities counter the presentation gains, and the supplied PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
